chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad informed me, saying: Abul Abbas al-Saraj informed us, saying: Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Ajlan narrated from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Beware of obscene language, for indeed Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, does not like the vulgar person who uses obscene language. And beware of oppression, for indeed oppression in the sight of Allah is the darknesses on the Day of Resurrection. And beware of stinginess, for it led those who were before you to shed their blood, and it led them to sever their kinship ties, and it led them to violate and make permissible their prohibitions.

key_terms.فَاحِش: A person who uses obscene language
key_terms.مُتَفَحِّش: One who is accustomed to or proud of obscenity

ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics warned against in this hadith from al-Khisal?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Khisal, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) links moral decay to three root vices: obscene speech (fahsh), oppression (zulm), and stinginess (shuh). Shaykh al-Saduq highlights how stinginess, in particular, acts as a catalyst for broader societal collapse, leading to bloodshed, severed kinship ties, and the violation of divine prohibitions. This triad reflects the Shia emphasis on purifying the self (tazkiyah) as a prerequisite for communal justice.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-235 Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad narrated that Abul Abbas al-Suraj quoted Qutaybat, on the authority of Bakr ibn Ajlan , on the authority of Sa’id al-Moqbery, on the authority of Abi Hurayrih that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,

“Beware of using obscene language, since the Honorable the Exalted God doesn’t like a vulgar person who uses obscene language. Beware of oppression, since oppression in the opinion of the Honorable the Exalted God is like the darkness of the Resurrection Day. Beware of stinginess coupled with greed, since it led those before you to shed blood; severe their bonds of kinship; devour illegitimately earned property; and be overly permissive regarding their women.”
